title: Agency Baking Support Staff
category: Computer Science, Accounting/Finance, Accounting, Business Economics, Business Administration, Banking
description:
Role Summary
To facilitate customer bill-information inquiries and bill-payment transactions through Azizi Bank’s approved POS devices, ensuring accurate transaction processing, proper customer verification, compliance with the Bank’s procedures, effective customer service, and timely reporting of operational issues.
The position is responsible for assisting customers with bill payments, retrieving and verifying bill information, processing transactions through the approved payment channels, issuing transaction receipts, and escalating failed, declined, or uncertain transactions to the relevant supervisor or support team.

Duties and Responsibilities
POS Device Operations and Bill Payments
Operate the assigned POS device and access the approved application using authorized credentials.
Accurately enter the bill number or scan the bill barcode, as supported by the device.
Verify the displayed bill details with the customer’s bill before proceeding, including the biller, bill reference, and payable amount where displayed.
Proceed with the payment only after confirming the bill information with the customer.
Customer shall Enter the card PIN only when required by the POS workflow and ensure that the customer’s PIN remains confidential.
Review the final transaction response displayed by the POS device.
Provide the printed receipt to the customer for successfully completed transactions and keep one receipt with itself
Additional Key Responsibilities – Cash-In and Cash Handling
· Process Cash-In and bill payment transactions through authorized POS devices in accordance with the Bank’s approved procedures and transaction limits.
· Verify transaction details, accurately count cash received, and confirm successful transactions before issuing receipts.
· Safeguard cash, maintain accurate transaction records, and reconcile physical cash against POS records daily.
· Immediately report cash discrepancies, failed or pending transactions, and suspected fraud to the designated supervisor.
· Ensure timely settlement and handover of cash through authorized procedures.
· Protect customer information and never disclose PINs, share credentials, or process unauthorized transactions.
B. Transaction Monitoring and Exception Handling
Monitor the status of each bill-payment transaction and ensure that the final response is checked before closing the customer interaction.
Distinguish between an explicit transaction failure and a timeout or missing response.
For a transaction returning an explicit APS failure, follow the Bank’s approved reversal procedure and applicable transaction rules.
For a timeout, missing acknowledgement, or uncertain transaction status, mark or report the transaction as suspect in accordance with the approved procedure.
Report cases involving possible customer debit, missing confirmation, duplicate payment, incorrect bill information, or receipt discrepancies to the designated supervisor or support team.
Cooperate with the Operations, ADC, IT, and other authorized teams during investigation and reconciliation.
Maintain transaction references, dates, amounts, POS identifiers, response messages, and other relevant details required for investigation.
C. Customer Service and Assistance
Explain the bill-payment process to customers in a clear and professional manner.
Assist customers in identifying the correct biller, entering bill references, and understanding the information displayed on the POS device.
Confirm the bill details with the customer before submitting the payment.
Provide the customer with the transaction receipt and explain its importance for future inquiries.
Handle customer complaints professionally and refer unresolved matters to the appropriate support channel.
Protect customer information and maintain confidentiality throughout the transaction.
Refrain from requesting, recording, disclosing, or retaining customer PINs or other confidential authentication information.
D. POS Device and Operational Security
Keep the assigned POS device, accessories, and any authorized supporting equipment secure and in good working condition.
Ensure the device is charged, connected, and ready for authorized transactions.
Protect device credentials and prevent unauthorized individuals from accessing the POS application.
Report device malfunction, application errors, connectivity issues, suspected tampering, loss, theft, or unauthorized access immediately.
Use the POS device exclusively for approved Bank services and authorized transactions.
Follow the Bank’s information security, customer confidentiality, and device-handling requirements.
Maintain custody of the assigned device and complete handover or return procedures when required.
F. Compliance and Internal Controls
Comply with the Bank’s approved POS operating procedures, bill-payment instructions, customer service standards, and applicable internal controls.
Follow applicable Know Your Customer (KYC), Anti-Money Laundering (AML), counter-fraud, and other compliance requirements relevant to the assigned duties.
Never bypass system controls, share credentials, falsify transaction records, or make unauthorized adjustments.
Immediately report suspected misconduct, fraud, security breaches, or violations of Bank procedures.

Job Requirements
Required Qualifications and Experience
Minimum educational qualification: High school certificate; additional education in business, banking, finance, accounting, or having diploma, CIT, DIT and BCS an advantage.
Previous experience in banking, agent banking, POS operations, bill collection, payment services, cash handling, or customer service is preferred.
Basic computer and digital-device operating skills.
Ability to read and accurately enter bill numbers, transaction references, and amounts.
Good communication and customer-handling skills.
Fluency in the local languages required for the assigned service area; Dari and/or Pashto proficiency is essential according to the location.
Willingness to work in the field and visit assigned agent outlets or service locations, where applicable.
4. Required Knowledge and Competencies
Digital Banking Knowledge: Basic knowledge of digital banking services, including ATMs, debit and prepaid cards, MasterCard services, and mobile wallets, with the ability to guide customers on their use.
POS device operation and basic troubleshooting.
Understanding of successful, declined, failed, and timed-out transactions.
Accuracy, attention to detail, and procedural discipline.
Customer service and complaint handling.
Confidentiality, information security, and fraud awareness.
Basic transaction recordkeeping and reporting.
Communication, teamwork, accountability, and timely escalation.

Submission Guidelines
Kindly Apply through jobs.af ATS ,and all the CV's should be submitted on Thursday before 10:00AM.

title: Agency Banking Support Staff
category: Computer Science, Accounting/Finance, Accounting, Business Economics, Administrative, Business Administration, Banking
description:
Role Summary
To facilitate customer bill-information inquiries and bill-payment transactions through Azizi Bank’s approved POS devices, ensuring accurate transaction processing, proper customer verification, compliance with the Bank’s procedures, effective customer service, and timely reporting of operational issues.
The position is responsible for assisting customers with bill payments, retrieving and verifying bill information, processing transactions through the approved payment channels, issuing transaction receipts, and escalating failed, declined, or uncertain transactions to the relevant supervisor or support team.

Duties and Responsibilities
A. POS Device Operations and Bill Payments
Operate the assigned POS device and access the approved application using authorized credentials.
Accurately enter the bill number or scan the bill barcode, as supported by the device.
Verify the displayed bill details with the customer’s bill before proceeding, including the biller, bill reference, and payable amount where displayed.
Proceed with the payment only after confirming the bill information with the customer.
Customer shall Enter the card PIN only when required by the POS workflow and ensure that the customer’s PIN remains confidential.
Review the final transaction response displayed by the POS device.
Provide the printed receipt to the customer for successfully completed transactions and keep one receipt with itself
Additional Key Responsibilities – Cash-In and Cash Handling
· Process Cash-In and bill payment transactions through authorized POS devices in accordance with the Bank’s approved procedures and transaction limits.
· Verify transaction details, accurately count cash received, and confirm successful transactions before issuing receipts.
· Safeguard cash, maintain accurate transaction records, and reconcile physical cash against POS records daily.
· Immediately report cash discrepancies, failed or pending transactions, and suspected fraud to the designated supervisor.
· Ensure timely settlement and handover of cash through authorized procedures.
· Protect customer information and never disclose PINs, share credentials, or process unauthorized transactions.
B. Transaction Monitoring and Exception Handling
Monitor the status of each bill-payment transaction and ensure that the final response is checked before closing the customer interaction.
Distinguish between an explicit transaction failure and a timeout or missing response.
For a transaction returning an explicit APS failure, follow the Bank’s approved reversal procedure and applicable transaction rules.
For a timeout, missing acknowledgement, or uncertain transaction status, mark or report the transaction as suspect in accordance with the approved procedure.
Report cases involving possible customer debit, missing confirmation, duplicate payment, incorrect bill information, or receipt discrepancies to the designated supervisor or support team.
Cooperate with the Operations, ADC, IT, and other authorized teams during investigation and reconciliation.
Maintain transaction references, dates, amounts, POS identifiers, response messages, and other relevant details required for investigation.
C. Customer Service and Assistance
Explain the bill-payment process to customers in a clear and professional manner.
Assist customers in identifying the correct biller, entering bill references, and understanding the information displayed on the POS device.
Confirm the bill details with the customer before submitting the payment.
Provide the customer with the transaction receipt and explain its importance for future inquiries.
Handle customer complaints professionally and refer unresolved matters to the appropriate support channel.
Protect customer information and maintain confidentiality throughout the transaction.
Refrain from requesting, recording, disclosing, or retaining customer PINs or other confidential authentication information.
D. POS Device and Operational Security
Keep the assigned POS device, accessories, and any authorized supporting equipment secure and in good working condition.
Ensure the device is charged, connected, and ready for authorized transactions.
Protect device credentials and prevent unauthorized individuals from accessing the POS application.
Report device malfunction, application errors, connectivity issues, suspected tampering, loss, theft, or unauthorized access immediately.
Use the POS device exclusively for approved Bank services and authorized transactions.
Follow the Bank’s information security, customer confidentiality, and device-handling requirements.
Maintain custody of the assigned device and complete handover or return procedures when required.
F. Compliance and Internal Controls
Comply with the Bank’s approved POS operating procedures, bill-payment instructions, customer service standards, and applicable internal controls.
Follow applicable Know Your Customer (KYC), Anti-Money Laundering (AML), counter-fraud, and other compliance requirements relevant to the assigned duties.
Never bypass system controls, share credentials, falsify transaction records, or make unauthorized adjustments.
Immediately report suspected misconduct, fraud, security breaches, or violations of Bank procedures.

Previous experience in banking, agent banking, POS operations, bill collection, payment services, cash handling, or customer service is preferred.

title: Graphic Designer & IT Officer
description:
Job Summary
Job Purpose:
The Graphic Designer & IT Officer will provide day-to-day IT and graphic design support to the organization. The position will ensure that staff have reliable access to computers, printers, scanners, internet and other IT services, while also producing quality communication, branding, IEC and multimedia materials.
Key Responsibilities
1. IT Support and Systems
Provide first-line technical support to staff for computer, software, printer, scanner, internet, Wi-Fi and other IT-related issues.
Install, configure, update and maintain computers, software, antivirus and other IT equipment.
Troubleshoot hardware, software, network and connectivity problems and coordinate with external service providers when required.
Manage user accounts, email systems, software updates and basic system administration.
Maintain IT equipment and asset records and keep track of repairs, maintenance and replacements.
Provide basic guidance to staff on the safe and effective use of IT systems and equipment.
2. Backup, Data Security and Maintenance
Develop and maintain a reliable backup system for important organizational and projects data.
Conduct regular backups and periodically test data recovery to ensure information can be restored when needed.
Maintain appropriate access controls and support data protection and information security.
Recommend improvements to data storage, backup, equipment and IT systems.
3. Graphic Design and Branding
Develop and maintain the organization's branding system, including templates, logos, colors, fonts and other visual identity materials.
Design brochures, flyers, posters, banners, infographics, certificates, presentations, reports, social media graphics and other communication materials.
Develop IEC and visibility materials for project, awareness sessions, trainings and community engagement.
Ensure all materials are consistent with organizational branding and, where applicable, donor requirements.
Coordinate with printing and other vendors when required and review final products before printing.
4. Photography and Video
Capture photographs and videos during organizational events, field visits, trainings and project activities.
Edit photographs and videos for social media, reports, presentations, training materials and other communication purposes.
Prepare and subtitle videos where required.
Ensure timely collection of photographs and videos from field teams and staff.
Organize, archive and safely back up photographs, videos and other digital media.
Ensure appropriate photo/video consent is obtained and documented in accordance with organizational policies.
Perform any other relevant duties assigned by the supervisor.

Job Requirements
Required Qualifications and Experience
Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Graphic Design, Communications or a related field.
At least 2 years of relevant experience in IT support, graphic design, communications or a combined role.

Good knowledge of computer hardware, software, networks, internet troubleshooting and data backup.
Good knowledge of graphic design software such as Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, Premier and/or InDesign.
Experience in photography, video editing and digital content production.
Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly PowerPoint.
Strong organizational, communication and problem-solving skills.
Fluency in English and good knowledge of Dari and/or Pashto.

title: Technical Team Leader
description:
Role Summary
We are looking for a qualified and motivated Technical Team Leader to oversee and drive our wireless network operations.
In this role, you will lead a technical team in the installation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of wireless and microwave network equipment, ensuring reliable connectivity and exceptional service delivery. The ideal candidate combines strong technical expertise in RF, IP networking, and wireless systems with proven leadership and communication skills to achieve operational excellence in ISP field operations.

Duties and Responsibilities
Team Lead & Operations
Lead and supervise the technical team in daily field operations, ensuring efficiency, professionalism, and timely task completion.
Coordinate technical resources for wireless and microwave network installations, maintenance, and troubleshooting.
Provide remote and on-site technical support to field technicians and clients.
Track and manage customer issues through the UCRM Helpdesk, ensuring timely resolution and proper follow-up.
Monitor and maintain Customer Premises Equipment (CPEs) and network devices through AirControl or other management systems.
Prepare and submit comprehensive daily, weekly, and monthly reports summarizing operational performance and key updates.
Microwave Systems
Execute the installation, activation, and troubleshooting of microwave links following established protocols.
Perform Radio Frequency (RF) testing, signal analysis, and alignment to ensure optimal performance.
Conduct site surveys to determine optimal equipment placement, line-of-sight, and signal strength.
Troubleshoot and repair microwave radio equipment and related components.
Conduct surveys for Microwave projects, arrange requirements, and implement technical solutions as needed.
Take full responsibility for all microwave-related field activities and knowledge transfer to the team.
Wireless Systems
Installation and deployment of UAT and customer wireless network equipment.
Ensure installed wireless equipment is fully functional and optimized for performance.
Document and share technical solutions to improve team knowledge and future efficiency.
LAN & Network Support
Oversee the installation and configuration of LAN network devices to meet customer and project requirements.
Troubleshooting network infrastructure issues for both internal systems and customer environments.
Collaborate with NOC, CRM, and Helpdesk teams to ensure end-to-end service reliability.

Job Requirements
Bachelor’s or equivalent degree in Computer Science (BCS), Information Technology (BIT), or a related field.
Minimum 3 years of experience in IT, networking, or ISP operations, preferably within the telecommunications sector, with hands-on experience in wireless and microwave networks.
Certifications such as CWNP/CWNA, CCNP/CCNA, and MCITP are highly preferred and will be an added advantage.
Strong understanding of RF principles and microwave transmission technologies.
Expertise in wireless network system and equipment, LAN/WAN infrastructure, IP addressing, VLANs, routing, and Layer 2/3 switching.
Hands-on experience with Cisco devices, network troubleshooting, and network monitoring tools.
Ability to configure, deploy, and maintain new wireless or network equipment efficiently.
Strong leadership and team management abilities with excellent communication skills in both English and the local language.
Excellent Problem-solving, analytical, and decision-making abilities.

Record and manage customer complaint history in the designated system, ensuring continuous follow-up until full resolution.

Monitor network performance tools (Red EMCO) for microwave and InfiNet devices, including ping latency and interference analysis, and support corrective actions to ensure timely issue resolution.
Monitor Air Control Alerting systems for network devices including device online/offline status, pole movement alerts, interference issues, hotspot connectivity failures, CCQ degradation, and bitrate issues, and take corrective or escalated action as required.

Resolve customer-side issues related to CPE (Customer Premises Equipment) and LAN networks using remote access tools.

Identify, analyze, and resolve customer connectivity issues remotely using diagnostic and remote support tools.

Record and manage demo customers’ complaints and ensure follow-up until resolution in the designated system.

Update internal communication groups (e.g., WhatsApp groups) for new installations, link termination, and network incident notifications, and inform customers of urgent technical issues when required.
Coordinate and arrange field teams for on-site visits when remote troubleshooting is not sufficient.

Respond to all customer inquiries, calls, emails, and complaints in a professional and timely manner.
Communicate planned and unplanned maintenance activities, outages, and service issues to customers via email, phone, or messaging platforms, ensuring confirmation and status updates.

title: Ethical Conduct and Humanitarian Health Systems Standards Officer (Re Announced)
description:
About CTG
CTG was established in 2006, almost 20 years ago, in Afghanistan. We currently operate in 35 countries and have approximately 11,500 staff members committed to good!
But do you know who we are? And what do we do?
We provide tailored Human Resources and Staffing Solutions that support critical global initiatives across Humanitarian and Development sectors, and are now strategically foraying into new industries, including Construction, Energy, and IT, with a focus on high-risk regions.
Here’s a list of services we offer:
•Staffing solutions and HR management services
•Monitoring and evaluation
•Fleet management and logistics
•Facilities management
•Sustainability and Communications Advisory
•Election monitoring and observation
•IT professional services
•Medical assistance
Visit www.ctg.org to find out more.

Job Descriptions
Background: Our client in Afghanistan provides technical assistance to the Ministry of Public Health (MoPH) and health sector partners to support the delivery of safe, ethical, and people-centered health services in humanitarian and development settings. In a complex operating environment, upholding ethical conduct and accountability is essential to ensure safe access to health services for communities and dignified, professional service delivery by health workers. All support is provided in line with the Do No Harm principle and our client framework for technical engagement with national health systems.
Purpose of the Position
This consultancy supports efforts to strengthen ethical conduct and professional behavior across the health sector by identifying gaps and opportunities to better align policies, practices, and operational systems with international minimum standards. This is a consultancy position reporting directly to our client under the technical supervision of the designated our client Technical Lead. The consultant will work in close coordination with the MoPH General Directorate of Policy and Planning, while maintaining full our client reporting, accountability, and oversight arrangements.

Job Requirements
Key Responsibilities
The consultant will:
· Identify gaps and opportunities within existing MOPH systems, practices, and operational frameworks to strengthen alignment with international minimum standards in humanitarian and development settings.
· Develop a risk-informed roadmap and prioritized action plan with clear milestones and timelines.
· Provide technical support for the development and application of codes of conduct guiding health workforce behavior.
· Translate international standards into practical tools, SOPs, and operational guidance applicable to health service delivery.
· Design, develop, and deliver contextualized training and sensitization on ethical conduct, codes of conduct, and do no harm principles for health workers, implementing partners, and relevant MoPH counterparts.
· Support the integration of ethical conduct and minimum standards into onboarding processes and routine training systems.
· Provide technical guidance to support program-level implementation of standards at service delivery points.
· Promote community awareness on health rights, dignity, expected staff behavior, and safe access to health services.
· Maintain confidential data systems to track adherence to codes of conduct and minimum standards and produce analytical reports for our client and MoPH technical leadership.
· Strengthen the accessibility, visibility, and appropriate use of confidential reporting and feedback mechanisms.
· Support monitoring, supervision, follow-up, and corrective actions related to ethical conduct and minimum standards by health partners.
· Facilitate coordination with Health Cluster structures and PSEAH inter-agency mechanisms to strengthen alignment of standards, referral pathways, and response approaches.
· Serve as a technical focal point between our client, MoPH technical counterparts, and implementing partners to promote coherence and accountability in safe health service delivery.
Required Qualifications and Experience:
Education
· Bachelor’s degree in law, public health, social sciences, or a related field
Experience
· At least 5 years’ experience in health systems strengthening and application of ethical and minimum standards in humanitarian and development health settings, including experience in Afghanistan
· Proven experience in policy analysis, training, stakeholder engagement, and people-centered risk assessment and mitigation
· Strong understanding of international humanitarian and development standards, medical ethics, and Do No Harm principles
· Commitment to women’s and girls’ right to health
Language
· Fluency in English is a must and working knowledge of Pashto and/or Dari.
Knowledge and Core Competencies
· Strong analytical, coordination, and facilitation skills.
· Ability to work effectively in complex and high-risk environments.
· High standards of integrity, confidentiality, and accountability.
Additional Information
· At no stage of the recruitment process will CTG ask candidates for a fee. This includes during the application stage, interview, assessment and training.
· CTG has a zero tolerance to Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) which is outlined in its Code of Conduct. Protection from SEA is everyone’s responsibility

title: Software Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Ontario, Canada (Remote)
About CircleCI Engineering
CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them.
At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here.
Team-Agnostic Placement
We don't hire for a team. We hire for CircleCI. Where you land depends on where your strengths create the most leverage, and we figure that out together. You might own the CI pipeline experience, deploy and release tooling, notification infrastructure, monetization flows, AI agent surfaces, or the foundational web platform. The through line across all of it is the same: full-stack ownership, a high bar for craft, and work that directly shapes how tens of thousands of developers experience CircleCI every day.
What You'll Do
Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It’s not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how problems get approached and solved.
Invent new interfaces . Software delivery is being reinvented. Pipelines run autonomously, generate fixes, and surface results that need human judgment. The tools developers use to understand, trust, and act on that work don't exist yet. You'll define what they look like.
Own the full stack. Build features end-to-end in Go, React, and TypeScript. You don't hand off at a layer boundary. You own the outcome.
Obsess over craft. Reliability and responsiveness are design concerns, not afterthoughts. Care about how the interface holds up when stakes are high.
Champion observability. Use Honeycomb, Datadog, and Rollbar to understand and improve your systems. Operational data drives stability, not just incident response.
Pick up slack. You'll notice gaps and close them — not because you were asked, but because that's the standard we hold ourselves to.
What You'll Bring
AI-native engineering practices. You use AI tools daily and can speak to what you've built, where they changed your approach, and where they fall short.
A track record of shipping. You've built something real and put it in front of users. 3+ years of production full-stack experience.
Full-stack depth. Strong React and TypeScript. Comfortable owning backend services in Go: API design, data modeling, service integration.
System design. You think about architecture, not just features. You make conscious tradeoffs and document your reasoning.
Production mindset. Latency, responsiveness, and reliability are design concerns. You're comfortable operating services in a distributed environment.
Sound like you?
You've stopped waiting for AI to mature and are already building with it, not as a productivity trick, but as a core part of how you think about problems. You care about the product as much as the code. You're drawn to work where the patterns don't exist yet and the best answer requires you to invent it. If that's how you already operate, we want to talk.

$127,000 — $159,000 CAD

title: Disaster Risk Reduction and Early Warning Systems Specialist
company: Citizen Organization for Advocacy and Resilience, (COAR)
description:
Job Summary
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
The Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) Specialist will lead and provide technical support for the planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of DRR activities in Kandahar and Helmand provinces. The position aims to strengthen community resilience to hazards by supporting risk-informed planning, preparedness, mitigation, early warning, and community-based disaster risk management in line with COAR policies and project objectives.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Primary Responsibilities
• Plan, coordinate, and implement project DRR activities in accordance with approved work plans, budgets, timelines, project objectives, and UNDP standards and require-ments.
• Support community-based disaster risk reduction initiatives, including risk aware-ness, preparedness planning, mitigation measures, and resilience-building activities.
• Conduct field visits and provide technical guidance to project teams and communi-ties to ensure quality implementation and timely resolution of challenges.
• Conduct training sessions for community members in target districts on Early Warn-ing Systems (EWS), including hazard awareness, early warning messages, communi-cation channels, and appropriate actions to take before, during, and after emergen-cies.
2. Technical Support and Expertise
• Provide technical support for the installation, configuration, testing, and operational-ization of Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS) equipment and tools in the four target districts, in accordance with UNDP technical standards, specifications, and guidance.
• Coordinate with relevant technical stakeholders to ensure the proper installation, functionality, testing, and handover of MHEWS equipment, and support community members in its safe operation, basic maintenance, and use for timely early warning dissemination.
• Conduct or support hazard, vulnerability, capacity, and disaster-risk assessments in coordination with UNDP and relevant stakeholders; identify at-risk communities and priority needs.
• Support the development and implementation of community disaster risk manage-ment plans, preparedness measures, and locally appropriate risk-reduction actions, in line with project objectives.
• Contribute to early warning and early action activities, including community aware-ness, dissemination of warning information, and coordination of preparedness ac-tions.
3. Coordination and Collaboration
• Coordinate with relevant provincial and district authorities, including disaster man-agement and sectoral departments, as well as community leaders and local structures.
• Ensure effective coordination with the project donor at field, district, and provincial levels, maintain regular communication on implementation progress and operational challenges, and align project activities with agreed implementation arrangements.
• Maintain effective collaboration with COAR program, MEAL, finance, logistics, and other relevant teams to support integrated implementation and ensure compliance with UNDP project requirements.
• Engage NGOs, humanitarian actors, community-based organizations, and other stakeholders to promote information sharing, avoid duplication, and strengthen coor-dinated DRR action.
4. Monitoring and Reporting
• Collect, verify, and maintain accurate field data, activity records, benefi-ciary/community information, and supporting documentation in accordance with COAR procedures and donor reporting requirements.
• Monitor activity progress against approved plans and indicators; identify implemen-tation gaps, risks, lessons learned, and recommendations for improvement, and communicate significant issues to the line manager.
• Prepare timely and accurate field updates, activity reports, assessment findings, suc-cess stories, and other reports required by the line manager and in accordance with UNDP reporting requirements.
5. Adherence to Policies
• Comply with COAR policies, procedures, staff code of conduct, and all applicable project and donor requirements.
• Uphold safeguarding, child protection (where applicable), Prevention of Sexual Ex-ploitation and Abuse (PSEA), protection, inclusion, and do-no-harm principles in all activities.
• Ensure respectful, safe, and inclusive engagement with communities; maintain con-fidentiality and promptly report safeguarding concerns or suspected misconduct through approved channels.
6. Other Duties
• Support capacity-building sessions, community meetings, awareness campaigns, drills, and other activities relevant to the project’s DRR objectives.
• Ensure that project resources, MHEWS equipment, and materials are used responsi-bly, and that relevant installation, operation, maintenance, and handover records are properly maintained in accordance with project requirements and UNDP guidance.
• Perform other reasonable, job-related duties assigned by the line manager in line with the position’s responsibilities and project scope.

Job Requirements
QUALIFICATION AND SKILLS
• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Disaster Management, Environmental Science, Civil Engineering, Agriculture, environmental science, Development Studies, water resource management, or another relevant field. Relevant professional training in DRR, climate adaptation, and emergency preparedness is an advantage.
• Experience: At least 4 years of relevant experience in disaster risk reduction, community resilience, emergency preparedness, early warning, humanitarian or community-based programming. Experience working with communities and government authorities in Afghanistan is an advantage.
• Skills: Good knowledge of DRR concepts and community-based approaches; strong coordination, communication, facilitation, and report-writing skills; ability to collect and analyse field information; planning and problem-solving skills; proficiency in MS Office; fluency in Dari and/or Pashto. English-language skills are an advantage.

Submission Guideline
Interested and qualified candidates who are residents of Kandahar and Helmand provinces are highly encourage to apply.

**Infrastructure and Connectivity**

2. Investigate site-to-site IPsec VPN issues with the relevant network teams and service providers.
3. Analyse application, server, and database logs to identify the source of failures. - Maintain monitoring, alerting, backup verification, and documented restore checks.

1. Support controlled deployments and rollbacks using approved procedures.

Hands-on API testing and a working understanding of HTTP/HTTPS, JSON, authentication, permissions, and error handling.
Practical experience configuring or troubleshooting VPNs, firewalls, routing, and network connectivity.

title: Senior Full-Stack Developer - Marketplace Web & Mobile Platform
description:
Headquarters: Phoenix, Arizona
URL: https://adventuretravel365.com/
Senior Full-Stack Developer - Marketplace Web & Mobile Platform
We have a big idea, and we’re looking for a top-notch Senior Full-Stack Developer to help us bring it to life.
We’re building a new contractor referral and services marketplace, think Thumbtack or Angi , where clients can easily find and connect with contractors and service providers. The vision includes both an interactive web platform and mobile app, with everything from user accounts and referrals to job tracking, payments, advertising, and more.
This is a fully remote, full-time, ongoing position, and we’re open to applicants worldwide.
There are a lot of moving pieces, which is exactly why we’re looking for someone who has built something like this before and gets excited about taking a platform from an idea to a working product, then continuing to grow it with us.
What You’ll Help Us Build
The platform will have two main sides: clients looking for services and contractors/vendors looking for business.
Some of the functionality we’re planning includes:
Client and contractor/vendor accounts and profiles
Contractor listings, categories, search, and filtering
Service requests, inquiries, referrals, and lead management
Job and project tracking
Client and vendor dashboards
Online payments and transaction tracking
Reviews and ratings
Notifications and communications
Banner advertising and paid promotional opportunities
Admin tools for managing the platform
Reporting and analytics
Secure management of user, job, and transaction data
And probably more! We have a strong vision for where we want this to go, but we also want the right developer to help us determine the smartest way to build it.
This will be an evolving platform, so we’re looking for someone who wants to grow with it, not simply complete a checklist of features.
Who We’re Looking For
We’d love to find someone with strong experience in full-stack web and mobile development , especially someone who has worked on a marketplace, booking platform, service-provider network, or another multi-user platform.
You should be comfortable with:
Full-stack web development
Mobile or cross-platform app development
Strong front-end and back-end development
Multi-user marketplace platforms
User authentication and account management
Payment gateway integrations
Databases and APIs
Third-party integrations
Dashboards and reporting
Secure, scalable application architecture
Cloud hosting and deployment
Testing, maintenance, and optimization
Using modern AI-powered development tools and integrating AI capabilities into web and mobile applications
If you’ve worked on something similar to Thumbtack, Angi, TaskRabbit, Upwork, or another two-sided marketplace , we definitely want to hear about it.
More Than Just Coding
We’re not looking for someone who simply waits for a list of instructions and starts coding.
We want someone who can look at the big picture, ask the right questions, recommend the best technical approach, flag potential challenges, and help turn our ideas into a platform that’s intuitive, scalable, and built to grow.
You’ll also be expected to study established platforms like Thumbtack and Angi , understand how their user journeys and marketplace functionality work from both the client and service-provider sides, and use those learnings to help us determine the best approach for our own platform.
You should be able to take the project through planning, architecture, development, testing, launch, and beyond , while communicating clearly with a non-technical team along the way.
Strong spoken and written English communication skills are important. You should be comfortable discussing ideas, explaining technical decisions clearly, and communicating regularly with a non-technical team.

title: INFORMATION SYSTEMS OFFICER

description:
Org. Setting and Reporting
This position is located in the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) Kabul Main Office. The Information Systems Officer reports to the Chief of Unit, UNAMA Field Technology Section.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority and under the direct supervision of Chief FTS, the Information Systems Officer will perform the following responsibilities: • Plans and directs all major information systems projects within the mission, monitoring the progress of the systems analysis, design, development, testing and implementation of new, moderately complex systems, and/or, participates as a member of a team with responsibility for major components of the more complex systems; • Manages the budget of the Information Systems unit, formulating and monitoring budget allocations and expenditures, verifying funding and ensuring no overrun occurs; • Develops technical specifications for the procurement of equipment and contractual services, and coordinates the technical evaluation of offers and proposals received; • Develops and recommends strategies to implement global information systems projects originating out of DFS/ICTD and the mission; • Develops, implements and monitors information systems standards, guidelines and procedures; • Develops detailed systems and other functional specifications and user documentation for system as required; • Provides specialized advice to users, analysing users’ requirements and translating these into new applications; determines application systems integration and linkage issues; • Maintains, upgrades or enhances existing user systems; troubleshoots and provides continuing support, to include resolving difficult problems, advising on the use of new techniques, monitoring transactions to measure performance and continued effectiveness of assigned systems, etc; • Develops training materials, operating and user manuals; trains staff in assigned systems; • Develops disaster recovery plans relating to information systems and ensures appropriate planning and training of those responsible; • Researches, analyses and evaluates new technologies and makes recommendations for their deployment; • Participates in writing reports and papers on systems-related topics, system requirements, information strategy etc; • Provides professional leadership and work direction for the Unit, develops the yearly work plan, mentors and supervises personnel of the Unit. • Handles all aspects of contract administration including establishment of service level agreements with vendors and chargeback policy for users. • Provides guidance to, and may supervise, new/junior staff, consultants, etc. Internetworking & Infrastructure • Develops plans for major IT systems projects within the mission, monitoring the progress of the design, installation and commissioning of the various systems; • Leads the team in the operation and maintenance of internetworking systems that includes routers and switches, operating systems platforms, database management systems, servers, workstations, and related equipment; • Devises and administers disaster recovery plans; provides training for support staff to implement these plans to ensure optimal readiness; • Responsible for the proper implementation of backup and recovery procedures • Maintains a regular review of the network resources access control, data security, and server and data stores security systems; • Ensures all information security systems are properly configured and maintained • Oversees the user access control for network resources and overall network security. • Collects and analyzes data to identify trends or patterns and provides insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods to enable data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. • Ensure that requirements and background information used for data analysis are documented. Performs other related duties as required.
Competencies
Professionalism: Shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Commitment to implementing the goal of gender equality by ensuring the equal participation and full involvement of women and men in all aspects of work. Planning & Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies. Identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required. Allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work. Foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning. Monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary. Uses time efficiently. Technological Awareness: Keeps abreast of available technology. Understands applicability and limitations of technology to the work of the office. Actively seeks to apply technology to appropriate tasks. Shows willingness to learn new technology.
Education
Technical school, university and other courses and training programmes relating to the work. High school diploma or equivalent and certification/diploma in other supplemental academic qualifications, training in Information Systems is required. Information System Security Professional certification is required (CISSP). Cisco Certified Networking Professional certification is required (CCNP). Additional Industry training and certifications are desirable.
Job - Specific Qualification
Information System Security Professional certification (CISSP) is required. Cisco Certified Networking Professional certification (CCNP) is required.
Work Experience
At least ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in Information Systems and Technology, Telecommunications, or related area is required. Experience in developing ICT disaster recovery & ICT Security plans and performing related exercises is required. Experience working in a United Nations common system field operation (inclusive of peacekeeping, political missions and UN agencies, funds, and programmes) – or similar international organisation or non-governmental organisation – in a conflict or post-conflict setting is desirable. Experience in carrying out programmatic/administrative tasks necessary for the functioning of the Unit including preparation of cost estimates/budgets, reporting on budget/programme performance, and recruitment of staff is desirable.

Please note that pursuant to the Staff selection system policy (ST/AI/2025/2): (1) Applicants for positions in the Field Service category cannot be of the nationality of the country where the position is located, and (2) Applicants for positions in the Professional and higher categories in a mission, field operation, or resident coordinator’s office cannot be of the nationality of the country where the position is located. For currently serving staff of a United Nations Common System organization, only the UN-recognized nationality will be considered for the purposes of these restrictions.
United Nations Considerations
According to article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. Candidates will not be considered for employment with the United Nations if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. The term “sexual exploitation” means any actual or attempted abuse of a position of vulnerability, differential power, or trust, for sexual purposes, including, but not limited to, profiting monetarily, socially or politically from the sexual exploitation of another. The term “sexual abuse” means the actual or threatened physical intrusion of a sexual nature, whether by force or under unequal or coercive conditions. The term “sexual harassment” means any unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature that might reasonably be expected or be perceived to cause offence or humiliation, when such conduct interferes with work, is made a condition of employment or creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment, and when the gravity of the conduct warrants the termination of the perpetrator’s working relationship. Candidates who have committed crimes other than minor traffic offences may not be considered for employment. Due regard will be paid to the importance of recruiting the staff on as wide a geographical basis as possible. The United Nations places no restrictions on the eligibility of men and women to participate in any capacity and under conditions of equality in its principal and subsidiary organs. The United Nations Secretariat is a non-smoking environment. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. By accepting a letter of appointment, staff members are subject to the authority of the Secretary-General, who may assign them to any of the activities or offices of the United Nations in accordance with staff regulation 1.2 (c). Further, staff members in the Professional and higher category up to and including the D-2 level and the Field Service category are normally required to move periodically to discharge functions in different duty stations under conditions established in ST/AI/2023/3 on Mobility, as may be amended or revised. The QA Engineer will work closely with the Project Manager, Resident Engineer, Contractor, and other members of the Consultant's team to ensure that construction works are implemented in accordance with approved drawings, BOQ, technical specifications, contract documents, approved materials, method statements, and required quality standards.
Key Responsibilities
Supervise and monitor construction and rehabilitation works on site from the Consultant's side.
Conduct regular site inspections and verify the quality and workmanship of completed and ongoing works.
Ensure that works are executed in accordance with approved drawings, BOQ, specifications, contract requirements, and approved methodologies.
Review Contractor's submittals , including Material Submittals, Method Statements, Shop Drawings, RFIs, Inspection Requests, and Test Reports.
Read and interpret architectural, structural, and MEP drawings and ensure their correct implementation on site.

Maintain proper records of inspections, measurements, instructions, photographs, test results, and corrective actions.
Assist the Consultant in reviewing Variation Orders, additional works, omissions, and quantity changes.
Coordinate with the Contractor's engineers and site team to resolve technical issues.
Participate in site meetings and provide technical input on construction and quality matters.
Ensure that rehabilitation works are properly executed considering the existing condition of the building.
Support the Consultant during project completion, snagging, handover, and Defects Liability Period inspections.
Specific Experience Required
Strong experience in building rehabilitation and renovation is a key requirement for this position. The candidate should have practical experience in projects such as:
School rehabilitation
Clinic/health facility rehabilitation
Hospital rehabilitation
Office and institutional building renovation
Building repair and maintenance
Structural and non-structural rehabilitation
Roof and waterproofing rehabilitation
Masonry, plastering, flooring and finishing works
Concrete repair and other civil rehabilitation works

Job Requirements
Job Requirements
Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering from a recognized university.
Minimum 5 years of relevant professional experience in construction supervision/site engineering.
Proven practical experience in building rehabilitation and renovation is required.
Previous experience working with a Consultant/Engineering Consultancy Firm in a supervision role is highly preferred.
Strong knowledge of construction drawings, BOQ, technical specifications, and construction methodologies.
Ability to review and evaluate Contractor's submittals and technical documents.
Ability to perform quantity verification, re-measurement, and secondary estimation.
Ability to identify construction deficiencies and provide appropriate technical guidance to the Contractor.
Experience in preparing site inspection, QA/QC, daily, weekly, and monthly reports.
Good knowledge of construction materials, testing procedures, and quality control requirements.
Good command of AutoCAD, MS Excel, and MS Word.
Good written and verbal communication skills.
Good English language skills , particularly technical writing and reporting.
Ability to work effectively in the field and coordinate with Contractors and project stakeholders.
Willingness to work at project sites, including remote locations.
Preferred Experience
Experience in UN, NGO, donor-funded, or international organization projects and previous experience working under international engineering/quality standards will be considered an advantage.
Important
This position is primarily field-based and focused on construction supervision and quality assurance. title: Senior Full Stack
description:
Headquarters: Tallinn, Estonia
URL: https://toggl.com/jobs/
We are looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer to join one of our Product Tribes, the cross-functional units that own the end-to-end experience for a specific Toggl user role. You'll join the Tribe building for managers, the people who plan work, protect margins, and keep projects on time and on budget.
You own significant parts of that experience end-to-end, working hands-on with product and design to ship work that matters. You'll do this as we build and launch Toggl 2.0, our consolidated planning, time tracking, and time intelligence product.
The salary for this position is €83,000 annually.
You can work from anywhere in the world as long as your main location is between UTC-4 and UTC+4.
The Role
As a Senior Full Stack Engineer, you own meaningful parts of the product end-to-end, from the data model and the API to the interface someone actually clicks: the technical approach, the quality of what ships, and whether it actually works for the people using it. You are accountable not for tickets closed, but for clarity, craft, and outcomes.
You'll work in the Tribe serving managers, across planning and capacity management, dashboards, and billable work. This is some of the most data-dense, interaction-heavy surface area in the product: schedules and capacity views, reports, and visualizations that have to stay fast and readable at real customer scale. The interesting problems live on both sides of the API here - the query behind a capacity view matters as much as how that view renders. You'll build with React and TypeScript on the frontend and our backend services (mostly Golang) and data layer (Postgres) behind them, alongside a product manager, a designer, and engineers who are used to owning their work and pushing back when something isn't right. In a tribe of 5 other engineers, your impact and visibility are high.
Our team meetings are scheduled between 11:00 and 16:00 UTC. Your availability and commitment to participate in these sessions are essential for effective collaboration and team alignment.
Your main responsibilities will be:
Ownership and delivery
Take projects from problem to production. Own the technical approach for major features front to back, break the work down sensibly, sequence it, and ship in slices rather than one big drop.
Make the technical calls in your area. Choose between options, name the tradeoffs, and decide without waiting for permission or escalating routine judgment.
Keep your work visible without being chased. Flag risks and slips early, keep the Tribe in the loop, and unblock yourself.
Craft and quality across the stack
Build interfaces people trust with dense, real-world data. Planning views, dashboards, and reports that stay fast, accessible, and readable when the dataset gets ugly.
Design the data and API layer those views depend on. Model it so the feature you're building now doesn't make the next three harder.
Own performance as a feature, end to end. Profile, measure, and fix the slow query and the slow render instead of hoping the data stays small.
Write code others can work in. Sensible components and services, real test coverage where it earns its keep, and a codebase that's easier to change after you touch it.
Working with product and design
Shape solutions, don't just implement them. Push on the problem, question requirements that don't hold up, and propose simpler paths when you see one.
Partner closely with design. Prototype early, spot the edge cases in a flow before it's built, and hold the bar on UX quality with your designer rather than after handoff.
Stay close to users and evidence. Join user tests, read the feedback, look at the data, and let it change what you build.
Raising the bar
Review code with intent. Give precise, actionable feedback that makes the change and the person better.
Mentor and interview. Help other engineers grow, and help us hire well.

title: Information Management Officer (Education) (NO-2), FT, #00138039, Kabul - Afghanistan, APR (For nationals of Afghanistan only)
description:
The post holder is responsible for supporting the information management (IM) function to enable the effective functioning of the Cluster Working Group at the sub-national level, and the achievement of the core cluster functions, throughout the Humanitarian Programme Cycle (HPC) in order to facilitate a timely and effective Cluster Working Group response.The IM Officer contributes to effective coordination between sub-national and national Education Cluster coordination structures and supports information management processes related to humanitarian needs analysis, response monitoring, partner mapping, gap analysis and humanitarian reporting. The position also supports strengthened information sharing and operational alignment across humanitarian and Basic Human Needs coordination platforms within the evolving coordination architecture in Afghanistan.
UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.
At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.
UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package.
Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF.
For every child, the right to Education
How can you make a difference?
Humanitarian action is of fundamental importance to UNICEF and encompasses interventions aimed at saving lives, alleviating suffering, maintaining human dignity, and protecting the rights of affected populations wherever there are humanitarian needs, as well as interventions addressing underlying risks and causes of vulnerability to disasters, fragility and conflict. UNICEF’s humanitarian action is guided by the Core Commitments for Children in Humanitarian Action (CCCs) which set organizational, programmatic and operational commitments and benchmarks against which UNICEF holds itself accountable for the coverage, quality and equity of its humanitarian action and advocacy and which are mandatory for all UNICEF personnel.
Furthermore, UNICEF is committed to support humanitarian coordination through the cluster approach. Introduced as part of the humanitarian reform, the cluster approach aims at ensuring clear leadership, predictability and accountability in international responses to humanitarian emergencies by clarifying the division of labor among organizations and better defining their roles and responsibilities within the different sectors involved in the response. As a member of the IASC, UNICEF works along with national and local stakeholders (including national and local authorities, CSOs, and communities) to support humanitarian coordination and to improve the collective impact of humanitarian response. Whether the cluster approach is activated or not, UNICEF plays a key role in both global and country-level interagency coordination for its areas of programmatic responsibility. As Cluster Lead Agency (CLA) for Nutrition, WASH, Education (co-led), and Child Protection Area of Responsibility (AoR) within the Protection Cluster, UNICEF is committed to fulfil the core functions defined by the IASC when the clusters are activated or when UNICEF is asked to support sectoral coordination.
A well-run Cluster Working Group coordination team, including Information Management (IM), is a formal deliverable of the Cluster Lead Agency and forms a part of the agency’s work. The IM Officer (Education Cluster) is a core member of the Cluster Working Group coordination team.
Within the evolving humanitarian and Basic Human Needs coordination architecture in Afghanistan, the IM Officer supports information management processes that strengthen evidence-based decision-making, coordinated humanitarian response planning, inter-sectoral analysis and operational coordination between sub-national and national coordination structures.
Purpose of the Job: Under the overall direction and guidance of the Education Manager/Specialist Cluster Coordinator, the IM Officer (Education Cluster) manages and supports the information management function of the Education Cluster Working Group at sub-national level. The incumbent supports the collection, analysis, management and dissemination of information required to enable evidence-based humanitarian planning, response coordination, monitoring and reporting.
The postholder's main tasks and responsibilities will include but not be limited to:
Coordination and Representation
As a member of the coordination team, contribute to the effective roll out and monitoring of the core cluster functions (as outlined by the IASC Reference Module) and to the Humanitarian Programme Cycle (HNO, HRP and CCPM),
Support the Cluster Working Group IM function and coordinate with others within the function to ensure effective communication, reporting and engagement,
Actively engage with other IMs through relevant IMWGs, including participating in the Cluster Working Group IMWG and representing the Cluster Working Group on the inter-cluster IMWG as relevant at sub-national level,
Promote harmonized and coordinated approaches to IM across partners, AoRs/ Clusters Working Groups and OCHA at sub-national level.
IM Function Support
Implement an IM strategy and data collection and analysis plan at sub-national level that take into account the information needs of stakeholders and that are compliant with standards and protocols for ethical data and information management and that is aligned with the national level IM strategy and plan,
Implement regular secondary data reviews and primary data collection including designing questionnaires using appropriate tools,
Conduct data processing including organizing, cleaning, triangulating, evaluating and validating the data,
Analyze data to meet identified information needs of sub-national Cluster Working Group members and other stakeholders,
Create accurate, quality and timely information products that are in line with agreed style guides,
Disseminate information and information products through appropriate channels,
Maintain and ensure the accessibility of a common and shared secure storage system,
Gather feedback on IM products and use them to make improvements.
Needs Assessment and Analysis
Working collaboratively with other members of the Cluster Working Group at national and sub-national level, contribute to the planning and implementation of needs assessment and analysis, including joint assessments and analysis, as requested,
Collect information on economic needs, markets and price monitoring to support the equal consideration and use of all programme delivery modalities (in-kind, cash, voucher and services) as relevant at sub-national level,
Work with sub-national Cluster Working Group participants to identify information gaps, agree and implement ways to bridge those gaps by providing technical support to partners,
Analyze needs assessment data to provide required information for the HNO including estimating People in Need (PIN),
Contribute to joint and inter-sectoral analysis processes and support alignment of needs analysis findings across clusters/sectors and relevant humanitarian and Basic Human Needs coordination platforms at sub-national level.
Strategic Response Planning
Implement partner presence mapping at sub-national level,
Contribute to strategic planning, response prioritization and development of humanitarian response plans and related analytical products, including support to objectives, indicators, targets, partner mapping and response monitoring.
Resource Mobilization
Monitor and analyze the sub-national Cluster Working Group’s financial situation and support financial tracking,
Support and advocate with Cluster Working Group partners for financial reporting on the Financial Tracking Service (FTS),
Support evidence-based advocacy and resource mobilization by providing accurate, relevant and timely data, information and information products.
Implementation and Monitoring
Implement and maintain a sub-national Cluster Working Group monitoring plan and associated databases, including a response monitoring (3/4/5Ws) database that is in line with and contributes to national level databases,
Ensure the sub-national Cluster Working Group monitoring plan, and 3/4/5Ws include programme delivery modalities (in-kind, cash, voucher and services),
Support sub-national Cluster Working Group members to contribute timely and quality periodic monitoring reports on Cluster Working Group and OCHA platforms,
Support monitoring in the areas of information flows, dissemination, processing, analysis and dissemination,
Contribute to quantitative and qualitative gaps and coverage analysis to identify spatial and temporal gaps, overlaps and coverage of the sub-national Cluster Working Group humanitarian response,
Monitor adherence to relevant sector quality standards, regulations and codes at sub-national level.
Operational Peer Review and Evaluation
Participate in the annual cluster coordination performance monitoring (CCPM) exercise and annual review,
Contribute to sectoral and broader humanitarian evaluations.
Accountability to Affected People
Be accountable to affected populations by encouraging the meaningful participation of affected people, maintaining an effective feedback mechanism and handling complaints appropriately, by ensuring data about the most vulnerable is systematically collected and analysed, and by encouraging partners to work accountably,
Ensure the inclusion of cross cutting issues (age, child protection, disability, gender, gender, gender-based violence (GBV) mitigation and response and HIV & AIDS) in Cluster Working Group data collection, analysis and dissemination,
Adhere to child safeguarding and PSEA policies including procedures for challenging and reporting incidents.
Strengthen National and Local Capacity
Support or implement actions to strengthen local and national leadership and capacity by encouraging participation of local and national actors in the IM activities of the sub-national Cluster Working Group and providing support to partners to overcome technical and operational challenges in participating in IM activities,
Implement an IM capacity assessment and capacity development plan for sub-national Cluster Working Group partners.
The IM Officer (Education Cluster) position is based in Afghanistan and supports the Education Cluster coordination function at sub-national or regional level. The position reports to the Education Manager/Specialist Cluster Coordinator (P3/P4) and supports information management, data analysis, reporting and coordination processes required for effective Education Cluster coordination and humanitarian response planning.
If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Information Management Officer, NO2, Job Description.pdf

Be Part of Building the Future
Dremio is the unified lakehouse platform for self-service analytics and AI, serving hundreds of global enterprises, including Maersk, Amazon, Regeneron, NetApp, and S&P Global. Customers rely on Dremio for cloud, hybrid, and on-prem lakehouses to power their data mesh, data warehouse migration, data virtualization, and unified data access use cases. About the role
Dremio’s Query Execution team builds the runtime responsible for executing analytical queries at scale. The team sits between query planning and table scans, owning the systems that turn query plans into efficient, reliable execution.
As a Senior Staff Software Engineer, you’ll work on query operators, expression evaluation, memory management, execution scheduling, runtime planning, and performance optimization. Your work will directly affect query performance, scalability, and reliability across Dremio’s cloud data platform.
What you’ll be doing
Build the execution engine: Design, implement, test, and support query operators, expression evaluation, execution scheduling, runtime planning, and resource management.
Improve runtime performance: Optimize vectorized processing, concurrency, parallelism, memory usage, data exchange, and disk spilling.
Diagnose difficult problems: Investigate query correctness and performance issues using query profiles, profiling tools, telemetry, benchmarks, logs, and production data.
Optimize Java and the JVM: Improve CPU utilization, allocation behavior, garbage collection, thread behavior, and other runtime characteristics.
Collaborate across the query engine: Work with Query Planner, Datalake, Product, Support, and field engineering teams on end-to-end query improvements.
Use AI-assisted development tools: Apply AI tools to code comprehension, debugging, test generation, documentation, and incident analysis.
Apply engineering judgment: Validate AI-generated code and recommendations through review, testing, benchmarking, and engineering judgment.
Raise the engineering bar: Participate in design and code reviews, contribute to technical direction, and mentor other engineers.
What we’re looking for
Software engineering experience: 5+ years developing production software, preferably in database systems, query execution, distributed systems, or related areas.
Programming skills: Strong Java skills; experience with C++ is a plus.
Computer science fundamentals: Strong foundation in data structures, algorithms, concurrency, multithreaded programming, and asynchronous programming.
Database and distributed systems knowledge: Understanding of database internals, query processing, distributed execution, and performance optimization.
Performance engineering experience: Experience profiling and optimizing CPU, memory, garbage collection, thread behavior, or other runtime characteristics.
Problem-solving ability: Ability to solve ambiguous technical problems and work effectively across team boundaries.
Engineering judgment: Ability to evaluate tradeoffs, validate solutions rigorously, and make sound decisions when working with unfamiliar or AI-assisted implementations.
Communication and ownership: Strong communication skills, a sense of ownership, and a commitment to delivering high-quality software.
Bonus points if you have
Query engines: Distributed query engines, database engines, or large-scale data processing systems.
Execution techniques: Vectorized execution, query operators, expression evaluation, code generation, or runtime optimization.
Runtime systems: JVM profiling, memory management, caching, networking, data exchange, execution scheduling, or disk spilling.

title: Principal Infrastructure Architect: Data Platform
description:
Headquarters: Remote
ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You’ll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won’t just contribute. You’ll make things happen–fast.
As a Principal Infrastructure Architect on our Infrastructure Architecture team, you will be the architecture team's partner to ZoomInfo's data engineering organization. Data engineering owns the platforms and the products built on them. You bring the infrastructure patterns, evaluation rigor, and cross-team alignment that help them build and run those platforms well on GCP.
This is a cloud architect seat with a data specialty. You bring the same cloud, Kubernetes, networking, and infrastructure-as-code foundation as the rest of the architecture team, plus enough hands-on depth in data systems to be credible with the engineers who run them.
The work breaks down four ways:
Patterns. You establish and maintain the paved-road patterns data teams build on: infrastructure as code, CI/CD for data jobs and pipelines, monitoring and alerting, performance, and cost. You keep them easy to consume and self-service.
Enablement and alignment. You help data teams adopt those patterns, review their designs, and work through hard infrastructure trade-offs with them.
Evaluation. You run POCs of new data technologies and vendor offerings as part of the procurement and technology-lifecycle process, and you write recommendations engineering leaders can act on.
Shared stewardship. You take a full share of the architecture team's general work: weekly architecture reviews across all domains, standards and ADRs, and infrastructure consulting for any team that needs it.
The data estate is broad. We don't expect deep experience across all of it. We expect real depth in some areas and the ability to build depth in others as the work demands. Patterns get adopted here through leadership and communication rather than positional authority. You'll write reference implementations, open the first PRs, and stay hands-on through enablement when a critical initiative calls for it.
What You'll Do
Establish infrastructure patterns for data workloads. Design and maintain reference patterns for provisioning and operating the data platforms ZoomInfo runs: streaming and messaging (Kafka/Confluent, Pub/Sub), operational databases (PostgreSQL/Cloud SQL, MongoDB), analytical stores (BigQuery, Snowflake), search (Elasticsearch/Solr), pipeline orchestration and processing (Apache Airflow/Cloud Composer, Dataflow/Apache Beam), and open table formats (Apache Iceberg). Ship them as Terraform modules, GitOps workflows, and documented standards that data teams can adopt without reinventing them.
Build the data paved road. Today's delivery tooling is application-centric. Define CI/CD and GitOps patterns for data jobs and pipelines, and partner with platform engineering and data engineering to make data delivery as safe and automated as application delivery.
Establish performance, cost, and observability patterns. Give data teams the patterns and guidance to run stores and pipelines efficiently (query and storage optimization, partitioning and clustering, tiering and retention, workload isolation, right-sizing) and the monitoring, alerting, and SLO practices that make performance and cost visible. Set the baseline patterns for backup, restore, and disaster recovery of data stores, including RTO/RPO targets. Partner with FinOps on data-layer spend. Review workloads with teams against these patterns and help them align.
